notes: status: verified = number taken from the listed source; needs_source = no reliable number found yet, fill before final build; game_defined = value chosen for gameplay, not from a source (list these in README).

objectives keys: sample = primary sample return, global = global properties, chem_map = chemistry and mineralogy map, yarkovsky = Yarkovsky effect, site = sampling site regolith documentation. Mapping of instruments to objectives is simplified for the game.
Data in this file was collected and organized with AI (Claude) and should be marked as AI-assisted in the README.

instruments.name: OCAMS camera suite (PolyCam, MapCam, SamCam)
instruments.note: Official mass and power not found. A secondary site (spaceflight101) says each camera is 0.6 kg and 5.3 W, but this could not be confirmed.

instruments.name: OLA laser altimeter
instruments.note: Mass = electronics 7.6 kg + optical head 13.8 kg (Table 3). Power 59 W nominal, 43 W standby.

instruments.name: OVIRS visible and infrared spectrometer
instruments.note: Abstract says 17.8 kg, Table 2 says 17.7 kg.

instruments.name: OTES thermal emission spectrometer
instruments.note: Linking OTES to the Yarkovsky objective (thermal data) is a game simplification.

instruments.name: REXIS X-ray imaging spectrometer (student-built)
instruments.note: 4.4 kg and 10.8 W are pre-flight current best estimates (CBE). eoPortal gives 2.7 kg. The NASA press kit says REXIS was a student collaboration with MIT and Harvard.

instruments.name: TAGSAM sampling arm
instruments.note: Arm length 3.35 m (NASA press kit). Mass and power not found.

instruments.name: Sample Return Capsule
instruments.note: 46 kg in both the NASA press kit and Lauretta et al. 2017.

solar_arrays.name: Large solar array
solar_arrays.note: Real reference: OSIRIS-REx arrays gave 1,226 to 3,000 W depending on Sun distance (NASA press kit). Lauretta et al. 2017 says 1,226 to 2,500 W.

antennas.name: High-gain antenna
antennas.note: 412 kbit/s downlink from Bennu distance during the April 2021 flyby (eoPortal). OSIRIS-REx used a MAVEN build-to-print HGA.

antennas.name: Low-gain antenna only
antennas.note: 10 percent of the HGA value, chosen for gameplay.

propulsion.note: OSIRIS-REx main thrusters were four MR-107S (eoPortal). Manufacturer spec sheet gives MR-107S Isp 225 to 236 s; 230 s is the middle value used in the game.

reference_spacecraft.note: Use dry mass 880 kg to tune the bus mass so the real OSIRIS-REx setup matches. 2,110 kg from NASA press kit, 2,105 kg from Lauretta et al. 2017.
